T4.9.message: 'Most printings read guṇātīta-rūpam' goes further than the evidence. Three witnesses read गुणातीतरूपम्: sanskritdocuments-vedasarast.md (a web e-text), vanivilas-1910-works-17.md and ramakrishna-math-mantrapushpam.md. Three read गणातीतरूपम्: gitapress-stotraratnavali.md, gitapress-shiv-stotra-ratnakar.md and brihat-stotra-ratnakar-wikisource.md. That is three against three, or two printed books against two independent ones (the two Gita Press books come from the same publisher). The evidence does not show a majority for either reading.
T4.9.suggested_fix: EN: 'Some printings read *guṇātīta-rūpam* … Others (the Gita Press editions and the Bṛhatstotraratnākara) have *gaṇātīta-rūpam* …'. HI: 'कुछ मुद्रित पाठों में *गुणातीत-रूपम्* है …'. In both, drop the word 'most'/'अधिकतर'.

T4.9.message: 'the line ends in *bhaje*' (HI: 'पंक्ति *भजे* … पर पूरी होती है') is wrong about the text. The verse as given in the bundle (verse.lines[3]) and every source excerpt (e.g. sanskritdocuments-vedasarast.md, vanivilas-1910-works-17.md) read 'भवानीकलत्रं भजे पञ्चवक्त्रम्'. The line ends in *pañcavaktram*, not *bhaje*. What bhaje ends is the run of six bh-words.
T4.9.suggested_fix: EN: '…and the run of *bh* closes on *bhaje*, "I worship".' HI: '…और *भ* की यह लड़ी *भजे*, "मैं भजता हूँ", पर पूरी होती है।'

T4.9.message: 'the two pull two ways: Śiva beyond every form, or Śiva in countless forms' (HI: 'हर रूप से परे शिव'). The reading guṇātīta-rūpam, as the same note glosses it, means 'His form lies beyond the three guṇas'. It says His form is beyond the guṇas, not that He is beyond every form. No excerpt (mw-gunatita.md: 'freed from or beyond all properties'; shvetashvatara-upanishad.md 6.11 nirguṇa) supports 'beyond every form'. This looks like an interpretive stretch. A human should decide whether it is acceptable framing.
T4.9.suggested_fix: EN: 'Śiva beyond all qualities, or Śiva in countless forms.' HI: 'गुणों से परे शिव, या अनगिनत रूपों वाले शिव।'
